title: Pricing by hours per project for hard floor care
audience: Owners and crew leads of hard floor care businesses who quote per job and need a price that covers labour, equipment, products and margin.
learningOutcomes: Calculate a cost per productive hour from the owner's own figures
Estimate project hours, including set-up, travel and checking time
Build a quote from hours, a rate and a margin, and state its basis and exclusions

instruction.heading: Why hours are the starting unit for floor work
instruction.body: Floor work is mostly time: the set-up and protection of the room, the preparation, each coat or pass, the drying time you plan for and the final check. Start from hours so that each quote shows its cost, its margin and the effect of a change in area or condition. Per-square-metre vendor ranges are references (Oneflare, undated), not your costs, and they cover polishing and sanding rather than routine cleaning.

instruction.heading: Build the cost per productive hour
instruction.body: Divide the year's total business costs by chargeable hours. Include wages with on-costs where you employ staff, plus vehicle running costs, floor machines and their servicing, abrasives and consumables, insurance and admin. Business.gov.au says on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure (1 October 2026). Xero Australia advises dividing by billable hours (3 September 2026). The research has no Australian figure for floor-care labour on-costs or equipment.

instruction.heading: Estimate the hours for each floor
instruction.body: Time each stage at a standard speed from your own jobs: protection, preparation, each coat or pass, drying checks and pack-down. Add travel, set-up and a checking pass as named lines. Add a set allowance for condition problems that show only once work starts, and say in the quote that it applies only when the condition is found. Xero Australia suggests 10 to 20 per cent for unexpected work, which is its own range and not a floor-care benchmark.

instruction.heading: Turn hours into a price and reconcile with the vendor range
instruction.body: Multiply crew hours by the cost per productive hour, then add a margin for the risk in the job, such as a difficult condition or a tight deadline. Then compare the result with the Oneflare ranges: the Victorian labour rate of $20 to $30 per square metre gives $1,000 to $1,500 for 50 square metres (CALC). Those ranges do not show the hours behind them. If your price differs, check your hours first, then the scope, and say which figure you used.

instruction.heading: Keep the quote honest
instruction.body: The quote states the area and how it was measured, the finish, the hours basis, the condition terms, the exclusions (for example, furniture moving or products the client supplies), the drying time and the validity date. Business Queensland suggests charging unplanned extra costs at cost plus a stated percentage; it suggests 15 per cent, which is a suggestion and not a benchmark (16 November 2022). Price any extra work in writing before doing it.

procedure: Gather the year's total costs and chargeable hours for the same period, with a source for each figure.
Divide total costs by chargeable hours and date the cost per productive hour.
Time each stage of a floor job at a standard speed, and record the times.
Add travel, set-up, pack-down and checking as named lines, and add a condition allowance only if the condition is found.
Multiply crew hours by the cost per productive hour, add the margin, then compare with the Oneflare ranges and state which one you used.
Write the quote with area, finish, hours basis, exclusions, drying time, client inputs and validity.
Record actual hours after each job and review the variance monthly.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A solo cleaner quotes a polish of a 50 square metre timber floor in good condition. Estimate: 12 crew-hours, including protection, preparation, two coats, drying checks and checking. Cost per productive hour is $55 (illustrative; not sourced). Target margin is 25 per cent of price (illustrative). Materials are excluded and shown as a separate line.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the labour cost and the price before materials, and how does the figure compare with the Oneflare labour range?
workedExamples.reasoning: The labour cost is 12 x $55, which is $660.00 (illustrative). A 25 per cent margin on price means the price is the cost divided by 0.75, which is $880.00 before materials (CALC). The Oneflare Victorian labour range for 50 square metres is $1,000 to $1,500 (vendor, undated; CALC). The cost-based figure is below that range, so the cleaner checks the 12 hours before quoting. If 12 hours is right, the vendor range is not the cleaner's price. If the hours are higher, the price rises with them. Floor check: at the award Level 1 adult minimum of $25.85 an hour with 25 per cent casual loading, which is $32.31 an hour (Fair Work Commission; 1 July 2025 variation), 12 hours is $387.72 before on-costs. That is a floor and not a cost per hour.

equipmentAndPpe: Time log for each job, with estimated and actual columns
Measuring tape or laser measure for area estimates

commonErrors.error: Pricing from the hourly wage alone.
commonErrors.prevention: Include on-costs, machine costs, abrasives, consumables, vehicle, insurance and admin in the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Leaving out protection, drying time or the checking pass.
commonErrors.prevention: Add each stage as a named line on every quote.

commonErrors.error: Pricing from a vendor per-square-metre range without its hours.
commonErrors.prevention: Build the price from your hours, then compare. Say which figure the quote uses.

commonErrors.error: Quoting with no area measurement, finish or exclusions.
commonErrors.prevention: State the measured area, the finish, the exclusions and the condition terms.

commonErrors.error: Never comparing estimated and actual hours.
commonErrors.prevention: Record actual hours for each floor, and review the variance monthly.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Pricing guidance only. The Australian Consumer Law applies to price statements, and the ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited (ACCC, 15 July 2026). State rules differ, so check your state's fair trading rules.

Where you employ workers, the Cleaning Services Award (MA000022) may set their minimum rates. The Level 1 adult minimum was $25.85 an hour, with a 25 per cent casual loading, from 1 July 2025. The 2026-27 rates were not checked. Whether this award covers floor-polishing work was not checked.
Keep a safety data sheet for each product, keep the original labels, use the PPE the SDS specifies and follow the label (Comcare). Dust and respirator rules for sanding were not researched.

qualityStandard: Each quote shows scope, hours or price basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
The cost per productive hour is calculated from the owner's own records and dated.
Actual hours are recorded for at least the first ten jobs of each type and compared with the estimate.
No quote is issued without a margin decision and a minimum-charge check.
documentationEvidence: Cost per productive hour worksheet, dated, with the source of each figure
Quote showing scope, hours basis, exclusions and validity
Job time log with estimated and actual hours
summary: Start every floor quote from timed work and a cost per chargeable hour.
Name each stage, the condition allowance and the drying time, and state the finish and exclusions in writing.
Gaps: floor-care equipment costs, sanding safety rules and 2026-27 award rates were not confirmed. The Oneflare ranges are references only.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which costs belong in the cost per productive hour for a floor-care crew?
options: Only the hourly wage of the lowest-paid worker
Wages with on-costs, machines, abrasives, consumables, vehicle, insurance and admin, divided by chargeable hours
The price the client pays, plus any deposit taken
The per-square-metre figure in a vendor guide

knowledgeChecks.question: A polish is estimated at 10 crew-hours and takes 13. What is the right response?
options: Record the actual hours, find the cause, and adjust the estimate and future quotes
Leave the estimate, because the client has paid
Cut the crew's breaks on the next job
Charge more to this client only and change nothing else

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a floor quote state its finish, area method and exclusions?
options: To show what the price covers, so extra work can be priced and disputes reduced
To make the quote longer for the client
To hide the margin from the client
To lower the client's expectations of the result

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. Supports: on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure.

Xero Australia, 'How to price services', https://www.xero.com/au/guides/how-to-price-services/, dated 3 September 2026. Supports: divide by billable hours, not total hours; add a set allowance for delays; the guide's 10 to 20 per cent range for unexpected work is the source's own figure.

Oneflare (Airtasker co-brand), 'Floor polishing cost', https://www.oneflare.com.au/costs/floor-polishing, undated ('2025 prices'). Vendor marketplace; covers polishing and sanding, not routine cleaning. Supports: per square metre ranges, state labour rates, finish prices, a poor-condition surcharge and whole-job totals.

Fair Work Commission, Cleaning Services Award (MA000022), https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000022.html, variation effective 1 July 2025. Supports: Level 1 adult minimum hourly rate of $25.85 and a 25 per cent casual loading. The 1 July 2026 position was not checked.

Comcare, 'Bathroom cleaning products', https://www.comcare.gov.au/office-safety-tool/spaces/bathrooms/bathroom-cleaning-products, no date shown. Supports: obtain the safety data sheet (SDS) for each product, keep original labels, use the PPE the SDS specifies, and follow label directions. The page covers bathroom products only.

ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, page last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading statements about prices are prohibited.

Business Queensland, 'Preparing a business quote: tips', https://www.business.qld.gov.au/running-business/marketing-sales/sales/preparing-quote/tips, last updated 16 November 2022. Queensland. Supports: list add-ons and alternatives on the quote; charge extra costs at cost plus a stated percentage (the source suggests 15 per cent, which is not a benchmark); follow up 7 to 14 days after the quote; confirm scope, capacity and deadline before quoting.

Notes: $55 an hour, the 12 hours and the 25 per cent margin are illustrative and not sourced. The $1,000 to $1,500 range is CALC on the Oneflare Victorian labour rate. The vendor figures are for polishing and sanding.
